meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (US-derived common law with customary law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: None concluded; principal international economic framework is the Compact of Free Association with the United States

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act (BCCA), Title 30 of the RMI Revised Code; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit regulations; beneficial ownership record-keeping and registered agent duties imposed by RMI company and AML/CFT rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Apostille states, RMI consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution authorizing formation of the RMI Business Corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and authenticated by Hague Apostille or RMI consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Biographical page of the ultimate beneficial owner's passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank letter on bank letterhead verified independently with the issuing bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and signatories against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and RMI domestic counter-financing of terrorism designations; PEP status must be disclosed and triggers enhanced due diligence; screening is performed by the licensed RMI registered agent before incorporation and refreshed periodically thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (filed exclusively through approved licensed registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in English/Roman script; the name must contain a corporate suffix such as Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, or a recognized abbreviation; names must be distinguishable from all existing names and reserved names on the registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a rejection, the applicant, through its licensed registered agent, must submit a written request for administrative reconsideration to the Registrar, attaching the name search report and any written consent from the holder of a similar name. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may file a judicial review petition in the RMI Civil Actions Court within 30 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a non-resident business corporation; no physical business premises in the RMI are required, and the statutory registered office may be the office address of the licensed registered agent. Online-only operations, including pre-order collections via Stripe and PayPal, are fully consistent with the non-resident corporate structure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability below 5% for this low-risk, non-licensed, non-resident merchant activity. A physical inspection would occur only in connection with a targeted AML/CFT investigation or a specific regulatory order.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act 1990, codified at Title 24, Chapter 1 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code (MIRC); key sections: 30 (registered office), 45 (registered agent), 47 (corporate powers), 53 (articles of incorporation), 60 (organization of corporation), 163 (annual franchise tax) and 167 (Registrar fees).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro; incorporation is filed by the incorporator or by a licensed registered agent acting on behalf of the non-resident entity.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BCA-1), with the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar upon acceptance and payment of fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. Shares may be issued for any lawful consideration approved by the Board of Directors; a standard authorized capital of 50,000 shares without par value is customary and attracts an annual franchise tax of USD 250 payable to the Registrar under 24 MIRC Ch. 1, sec. 163.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation approve the subscription and issuance of 1,000 shares of no par value common stock to the initial subscriber for the consideration approved by the Incorporator; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Corporation adopt the registered office at [address], Republic of the Marshall Islands, and ratify [Registered Agent] as registered agent; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the persons named on the Officer Appointment Schedule be appointed President, Secretary and Treasurer, with full authority to open bank accounts, execute operating documents, and file statutory reports; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Bylaws submitted to this meeting be adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Agent Engagement and Corporate Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed RMI registered agent (Majuro corporate services provider) acting on behalf of the Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the registered agent to conduct a name availability search against the Registrar's corporate index for the proposed corporate name ending in 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or an approved abbreviation. Confirm the agent's written consent to serve and its physical Majuro address as the registered office. Agree on the authorized share structure, usually 50,000 shares without par value, and complete client due diligence documents for directors and shareholders.
required_dossiers: Registered agent engagement letter and consent to act
Client due diligence questionnaire (KYC) with passport and proof of address for each director and shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as confusingly similar, the agent performs a second search and the applicant selects a distinguishable alternate name; the rejection notice identifies the conflicting entry, and the filing fee is not committed until name clearance is obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator (or licensed drafting counsel) executing the instrument for submission to the Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation under 24 MIRC Ch. 1, sec. 53, stating the corporate name, registered agent name, Majuro registered office address, authorized capital, the initial director(s) and, where applicable, the non-resident status of the entity. Obtain the incorporator's signature with notarization where required by the registered agent or opening bank. Confirm that the corporate purpose covers the manufacture of polyresin statues and garage kits under ISIC 3240.
required_dossiers: Signed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney or cover letter authorizing the registered agent to file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect notice, cure the stated deficiency (e.g., missing consent or incomplete purpose clause) and resubmit the corrected Articles within 30 days; no additional filing fee is charged for the first correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original Articles of Incorporation together with the statutory filing fee of USD 200 by bank draft or wire remittance through the registered agent. Optionally prepay the first-year annual franchise tax of USD 250. Obtain the Registrar's stamped receipt, file number and date-stamped copy as evidence of submission.
required_dossiers: Fee payment confirmation (bank draft or wire transfer)
Cover letter identifying the proposed file number and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for insufficiency, the applicant or agent files the missing document or amended page identified in the query notice within 10 business days; any fee shortfall must be settled before the certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and Certified Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the official commencement date and corporate registration number. Verify the certificate details against the approved Articles, and request certified copies and a Certificate of Good Standing for bank account opening and supplier contracting purposes.
required_dossiers: Stamped receipt of Articles of Incorporation
Request for certified copy and Certificate of Good Standing (if required by bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical variance from the approved Articles, submit a written correction request to the Registrar; the corrected certificate is reissued without reprocessing fee where the error is attributable to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Completion - Bylaws, First Board Resolution, Officers and Share Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial directors and corporate secretary of the newly incorporated Business Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting or act by unanimous written consent of the initial directors. Adopt the Bylaws, pass the First Board Resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption and officer appointments, execute the Officer Appointment Schedule, and issue the share certificate to the initial subscriber. Establish the statutory records and share ledger at the registered office or with the registered agent.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution or unanimous written consent
Officer Appointment Schedule and signed acceptances
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: De minimis omissions in organizational records are cured by a subsequent board written consent with retroactive ratification; failure to pay the annual franchise tax triggers the Registrar's statutory late fee and risk of administrative dissolution, which is remedied by payment of arrears and reinstatement under the BCA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business License Office, Ministry of Finance and Administration, Majuro; joint site clearance with the Environment Protection Authority (RMIEPA) and RMI Fire and Rescue Services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Manufacturing Business License under the Business License Act 1986; no special sectoral concession license is required for a polyresin statue garage-kit production operation, which is classified as general goods manufacturing under ISIC 3240.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMIEPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Environmental Registration (small workshop / garage-scale operation below the full EIA screening threshold); a Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required only if annual resin throughput exceeds RMIEPA screening thresholds or if effluent discharge is planned to the lagoon, shoreline or groundwater.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero liquid discharge of uncured resin, acetone wash water or sludge to the Majuro lagoon or groundwater; any on-site treatment must achieve pH 6.0-9.0 before reuse or disposal. Styrene and other VOC fugitive emissions must be captured by local exhaust ventilation, with workplace styrene exposure maintained below 20 ppm time-weighted average (ACGIH TLV) and no detectable odor at the property boundary. Uncured resin, catalyst, contaminated rags and empty drums must be managed as hazardous waste and shipped through a certified waste transporter under the RMI Solid and Hazardous Waste Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from RMI Fire and Rescue Services covering portable extinguishers, unobstructed egress and an approved flammable-liquid storage cabinet; structural loading clearance from the Public Works Department or a licensed engineer for mezzanine and pallet-racking loads; and Occupational Workplace Clearance from the Ministry of Health and Human Services covering local exhaust ventilation, nitrile gloves, organic-vapor respirators, eyewash station, and registration with the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration if employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Ministry of Finance, Majuro; Company registry: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (ORC) within the Attorney-General's Office, operating the official business registry portal at business.gov.mh. No separate income-tax authority exists for non-resident corporations because RMI imposes no direct national tax on them; customs matters are administered by the Customs Division, Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors incorporate under the Business Corporations Act 1990 (BCA) via a licensed registered agent; the ORC issues a Certificate of Incorporation bearing a unique Corporate Registration Number, which functions as the de facto statutory corporate/TIN identifier. No income-tax TIN or annual tax return is issued or required for non-resident status. A separate Customs Importer/Exporter Registration Number is obtained from the Customs Division, Ministry of Finance (Majuro port) when the corporation conducts physical importation of raw polyresin or export of finished statues; this registration is fee-based, renewable annually, and requires a local process agent for non-resident entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under BCA Section 104 and Title 54 of the RMI Revised Code, a Business Corporation may elect non-resident status at incorporation by maintaining at least 50% foreign ownership and no commercial activity sourced within RMI; non-resident BCs are statutorily exempt from all RMI income, franchise, capital gains, and withholding taxes. No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under domestic RMI law; classification is a binary resident/non-resident designation recorded on the ORC register. Hybrid outcomes arise only when a US parent makes a US federal 'check-the-box' election under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3; RMI has no income tax treaty with the United States, only a 2013 Tax Information Exchange Agreement, so no treaty-based hybrid rules apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None (No VAT/GST/Sales and Use Tax); revenue derived from RMI Customs Import Duty, license fees, and marine registry fees only
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — RMI levies no VAT/GST or sales tax, and no turnover threshold exists. Import duty registration under Customs (Development and Consolidation) Act 2013 is compulsory for any person importing goods into RMI, regardless of value; the annual business license (USD 100–500 depending on activity) under Chapter 9 of Title 35 is also mandatory for the Majuro business site if any local sales activity occurs, though a pure non-resident exporter operating via the ORC with no local premises ordinarily holds no RMI business license.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — the RMI has not implemented real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing APIs, digital tax stamping, or SAF-T reporting. Commercial invoices and bill of lading/airway bill remain paper or PDF-based; customs entries are processed manually or through the national single-window portal when available. No fiscal data exchange obligation applies to Stripe/PayPal prefunding or outward shipments.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Deemed zero-rated as outside the scope of any RMI consumption tax. RMI has no VAT regime, therefore exports of polyresin statues are not subject to any national indirect tax, and no registration or substantive approval is required to claim a zero rate. Exporters need only follow RMI Customs outward cargo manifest procedures under the Customs Act 2013 for goods leaving Majuro; statues exported physically must be documented on a standard Cargo Manifest/Export Declaration. Offshore export of digital or drop-shipped goods requires no RMI customs filing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Outward Cargo Manifest, as required by RMI Customs Act 2013)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical shipments from Majuro
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank Payment Record evidencing receipt of funds from the foreign buyer for the resin statue sale
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Because no VAT is levied, the primary compliance risk is fraudulent customs declarations or false claims of foreign-owned non-resident status to obtain RMI tax exemption. Under the RMI Customs Act 2013, a false declaration carries fines of up to USD 5,000 or three times the duty evaded, forfeiture of goods, and up to one year imprisonment; duty preferential claims (e.g., raw resin entered duty-free) are subject to retrospective clawback within 5 years. Misrepresenting the foreign-ownership facts to the Registrar of Corporations can trigger cancellation of tax-exempt status, restoration of all taxes avoided, and penalties under Title 54 for malicious false statements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Republic of the Marshall Islands (under the Financial Institutions Act 1987); U.S. Federal Reserve as de facto monetary authority due to formal dollarization — no domestic central bank or foreign exchange administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is sole legal tender, fully convertible de jure and de facto. The RMI operates a fully open capital account with no exchange controls, no prior-approval requirements on current or capital transactions, no dividend/profit remittance restrictions, and no withholding or repatriation charge for non-resident shareholders. Remittance flows are subject solely to bank-level AML/CFT screening and FATF-compliant transparency standards, not to governmental approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation applies. Because the domestic currency is identical to the export settlement currency (USD) and no central bank or FX administration exists, there is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio. Export proceeds may be retained in any commercial bank account or converted to third-country currencies at market rates via authorized correspondents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam – Marshall Islands Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-Low for treasury custody; High as a payment-collection switch. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise Multi-Currency, Airwallex) cannot lawfully establish deposit-taking relationships in RMI without a Financial Institutions Act banking licence. They may be engaged as non-deposit payment facilitators for e-commerce pre-orders (Stripe/PayPal settlement and payout into the RMI bank account), but final liquidity clearing must terminate in a licensed RMI-incorporated commercial bank or a recognized U.S. correspondent bank to avoid unauthorised deposit-taking and to preserve FATF-country transparency.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical presence and in-person verification interview is the default and strongly preferred compliance posture for first-time corporate account activation at RMI-incorporated banks. At least one director or a duly appointed authorised signatory holding a notarised and apostilled power-of-attorney must attend the initial meeting at the bank's Majuro branch. Remote video KYC may be permitted only for low-risk, non-resident entities with wholly transparent ultimate beneficial ownership and a pre-existing correspondent banking relationship; in such cases, certified hard-copy corporate documents must be couriered and a telephonic compliance interview is required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Business Corporation registered in a low-tax jurisdiction with no minimum capital paid in, raising substance and BO-transparency concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified charter/certificate of incorporation and registered agent certificate; full UBO register with passport copies; exemption from RMI income tax under Business Corporations Act (but active operation evidence required); executed Business Plan and financial projections; virtual office and substance records (licensed agent agreement, director resolutions); source-of-funds declaration with bank statements of contributing shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border e-commerce pre-sales and online payment volume via Stripe/PayPal without established physical trade history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce platform settlement reports and merchant ID; order-level ledger with customer contracts; raw material purchase orders and supplier invoices; shipment/customs/ISIC trade activity documentation; anti-money-laundering risk assessment matrix; ongoing transaction-monitoring and anomaly-reporting procedures prepared by the compliance officer; historical production and inventory documentation (casting log, inspection certificates, photos/video).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value outbound wires and FX forwards to resin suppliers in non-USD jurisdictions, appearing as large round-number disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices and packing lists; bank SWIFT MT103 copies; supplier due-diligence file; third-party logistics receipts; FX hedging master agreement and ISDA netting documentation; assurance of no sanctioned counterparties (OFAC sanctions screening log); audit trail from board-approved treasury policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity (or obtained loan) must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the funding bank to the RMI operational account. The wire shall use the memorandum line 'Capital Contribution – Business Corporation Equity / Subscribed Shares – ISIC 3240 Resin Statue Manufacturing' and include no ambiguous cash-reference terms. Purpose classification under a harmonised bank system should be 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' (BPM6 category DI, code AED/CF if required by correspondent). The bank verification package includes: shareholder resolution authorising the capital call, board resolution to open the account, executed share issuance register, UBO/source-of-funds declaration, and proof of economic activity (pre-order deposits, sales agreements). Wires in USD are unrestricted; no central bank approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and logistics payments are executed by SWIFT MT103 or, for confirmed purchase orders exceeding USD 250,000 per transaction, by an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (UCP 600) advised through a correspondent bank. For Chinese resin suppliers (CNY), a standard trade settlement through MT103 with invoice reference and commercial invoice attached is used. For EU prepress or painting-machine vendors, EUR disbursements are made through separate multi-currency sub-accounts, with contractual payment and FX settlement executed simultaneously to avoid market risk. All outbound wires are screened against OFAC and RMI sanctions lists; supporting trade documents are retained for exigency in a central data-room.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards on CNY/EUR/JPY against USD for firm commercial payables, via a licensed international bank with ISDA master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with restricted deliverability (e.g., CNY offshore CNH NDF) to hedge residual supplier exposures without physical delivery

Cross-currency swaps for interest or principal re-denomination on possibly mixed-currency capital loans, provided the swap is entered on an arm's-length basis and documented under a Credit Support Annex
Spot FX contracts for immediate conversion of trade receipts from payment rails (Stripe/PayPal settled in USD) into disbursement currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Annual Franchise Tax (Business Corporations Act combined statutory renewal filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 1 October; the filing window opens on 1 January of the same calendar year. For a newly incorporated Business Corporation, the first annual report is generally due by the next 1 October if incorporated before 1 July, otherwise by the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after 1 October attracts a monetary late penalty under the Registrar's fee schedule, with a statutory minimum penalty of US$100; continued non-payment of the annual report and franchise tax may lead to administrative dissolution after published notice, and reinstatement requires payment of all arrearages and penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent statutory audit is imposed on a tax-exempt non-resident Business Corporation under Marshall Islands law; any audit requirement must arise solely from shareholders, directors, or contractual counterparties. There are no size, revenue, or asset thresholds triggering a mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No RMI domestic GAAP is prescribed for non-resident Business Corporations; financial records may be maintained under IFRS or US GAAP. If an audit is voluntarily engaged, the auditors typically apply International Standards on Auditing or AICPA standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Marshall Islands law does not require an annual UBO confirmation return to the Registrar. Under AML/CFT and registered-agent practice, any transfer of or change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be notified to the registered agent promptly so the internal beneficial ownership register remains current; no public share-transfer filing deadline applies to the Registrar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$500 - US$1,200 per annum (registered office and registered agent inclusive)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; voluntary certified audit for a low-risk non-resident Business Corporation typically US$3,000 - US$8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective Marshall Islands corporate income tax burden. The Republic of the Marshall Islands has not enacted a corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or dividend withholding tax for non-resident domestic business corporations. No statutory tax holiday or preferential deduction regime exists because there is no corporate income tax base to incentivize. A non-resident BC that confines its business to offshore contracts, invoicing, payment routing, and foreign sales of resin statue garage kits is not subject to the Marshall Islands Business Privilege Tax. The only unavoidable annual state charges are registry franchise fees and registered agent fees. If the BC maintains an RMI office, RMI inventory, RMI employees, or direct sales to RMI customers, the RMI Business Privilege Tax may apply at the standard gross receipts rate of 3%, which is a gross-receipts tax and not an income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Marshall Islands corporate income tax return exists. A non-resident BC files the BCA Annual Corporation Report with the Register of Corporations through the Office of the Attorney General or the licensed registered agent's online filing portal; this is a corporate registry confirmation, not a tax return. The official filing currency is USD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; due on or before the statutory registry deadline prescribed by the Business Corporations Act for the BC's annual corporate report.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual registry filing deadline is determined by the corporate registry calendar and is not tied to the BC's chosen fiscal year-end. No corporate income tax return due date exists because no corporate income tax is imposed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name of the BC and its RMI corporate file number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact BCA-registered name and file number; designate the corporation as a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation if the current annual confirmation requires a status code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identity and street address in the Republic of the Marshall Islands of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident BC must maintain a licensed RMI registered agent and a physical registered office; a post office box is not acceptable as a registered street address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, residential addresses, and consent details for all directors and officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: RMI law does not require resident directors or a resident officer; non-resident individuals may serve. Provide full legal names and current addresses for the public register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized capital, issued shares, and principal shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum paid-up capital is required for an RMI BC. Disclose all registered shareholders and, where the registry form asks, beneficial ownership details for AML purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the corporation is not carrying on business within the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Sign this declaration only if the BC has no RMI office, RMI employees, RMI inventory, or RMI-source gross receipts. Signing falsely while conducting local business exposes the directors to BPT evasion liability and registry strike-off.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the Annual Corporation Report and to pay the annual registry fee by the statutory deadline triggers late filing penalties, loss of good standing, and administrative strike-off or revocation of the certificate of incorporation. Restoration requires payment of all accrued penalties, back fees, and Registrar restoration charges. Because no CIT return is required, there is no CIT late filing penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Business Privilege Tax Return, filed with the Revenue and Taxation Division of the RMI Ministry of Finance. This is mandatory only if the non-resident BC nevertheless conducts actual business activity within the Marshall Islands; for a purely offshore resin statue sales vehicle, the filing obligation is a zero-liability registration matter at most.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Periodic as prescribed by the Revenue Commissioner, typically monthly or quarterly depending on the taxpayer's classification and gross receipts level.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The BPT return and payment are due by the date stated in the taxpayer's BPT registration; the BPT is a gross-receipts tax assessed on business activity sourced to the Marshall Islands, not an income tax and not a tax on offshore sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total consideration, in USD, derived from business activities physically performed in or sourced to the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report USD zero for offshore pre-order sales of resin statue garage kits sold to non-RMI buyers and fulfilled outside the RMI. Include only RMI customer sales, RMI fulfillment sales, or locally performed services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Any deductions from gross receipts expressly allowed under the Tax and Customs Duty Act for BPT purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident BC claiming zero RMI gross receipts has no need of deductions; if local receipts exist, engage an RMI tax adviser to compute allowable deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed BPT liability at the applicable rate and authorized signatory certification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Sign only if the information is true. A false certification supports veil-piercing and personal liability of directors in BPT collection proceedings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the Tax and Customs Duty Act, failure to register for BPT, failure to file BPT returns, or failure to pay assessed BPT exposes the BC to monetary penalties, interest, seizure of assets, restraint of bank accounts, and loss of good standing with the Registrar of Corporations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - the Republic of the Marshall Islands does not impose dividend withholding tax on distributions made by a non-resident business corporation to its shareholders, regardless of the shareholder's country of residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement in force with any jurisdiction. There is therefore no RMI treaty-relief application procedure, no tax-residence certificate filing protocol, and no reduced withholding rate mechanism. Dividends, interest, and royalties may be paid gross from an RMI non-resident BC without RMI tax. RMI has entered into tax information exchange arrangements with some jurisdictions, but those instruments do not confer withholding tax relief. A shareholder seeking foreign tax credit relief must rely on the fact that no RMI tax was paid and must obtain a certificate of good standing from the RMI Registrar rather than a tax-residence certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest. Because no comprehensive DTA applies, no treaty rate is available. A non-resident BC may pay IP royalties for resin statue designs and intercompany debt interest free of RMI withholding tax; however, the recipient jurisdiction may impose its own withholding tax, CFC rules, or transfer pricing adjustments on those cross-border payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory local file, master file, or Country-by-Country Report threshold applies in USD for a Marshall Islands non-resident BC. The Marshall Islands has no corporate income tax, no transfer pricing statute, and no RMI CbCR filing obligation. Parent groups domiciled in jurisdictions implementing OECD BEPS Action 13 should apply their own group thresholds, commonly the EUR 850 million consolidated revenue threshold, but the RMI BC itself has no local transfer pricing return or documentation file to submit. The BC should nonetheless maintain intercompany agreements, pricing analyses, and board approvals to support the arm's-length nature of any related-party transactions in the group's home jurisdiction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Marshall Islands Economic Substance Regulations apply to RMI tax-resident entities carrying on specified geographically mobile activities such as banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters services, holding company activities, intellectual property holding, and distribution and service centers. The manufacture and online sale of resin statue garage kits is not a specified relevant activity, and a non-resident BC without RMI local trade is outside the ESR substance filing framework. Nevertheless, bank AML due diligence, UBO disclosure, and foreign tax enforcement require the BC to maintain genuine commercial substance: documented board minutes, separate bank accounts, fulfillment and subcontracting contracts, IP ownership records, records of decision-making, and a clear independence from the shareholder's home-country operations. A pure mailbox company will be reclassified by foreign tax authorities and will invite civil and criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Offshore Nominee Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Marshall Islands non-resident BC as a shell invoicing and profit-draining entity for resin statue pre-sales while management and control, product development, contract negotiation, risk assumption, and bank signatory authority remain in the beneficial owner's country of tax residence; failing to disclose the BC, its Stripe or PayPal payment balances, resin statue sales profits, and distributions to the ultimate tax authority; or using the BC to fragment a single integrated manufacturing and e-commerce business to avoid the home jurisdiction's income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI itself will not tax the BC, but the operating jurisdiction may assess unpaid income tax, interest, civil fraud penalties of up to 75% of the understatement, offshore disclosure penalties, and criminal fines. In the RMI, the Registrar may strike off the BC for filing a false annual non-resident declaration. In major OECD jurisdictions, willful offshore non-disclosure is a criminal tax offense carrying substantial fines and terms of imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil where the BC is the alter ego of the UBO. Directors and officers who sign false declarations, cause nominee filings, or control undisclosed payment accounts are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution, unpaid taxes, penalties, and costs. Travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition proceedings are commonly imposed in cross-border tax evasion investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and False Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the BC without real commercial activity: no board meetings, no decision-making records in the RMI, no substantive distribution or fulfillment contracts, no evidence of IP ownership and licensing control, all transactions executed solely by the UBO from another jurisdiction, and no commercial rationale for placing resin statue brand assets in the RMI entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the RMI Economic Substance Regulations, if the BC is reclassified as an in-scope relevant activity, the RMI competent authority may impose financial penalties, require remedial substance, and ultimately strike off the entity. Foreign tax agencies may treat the BC as tax-resident under their own management and control rules, subjecting all worldwide profits to full corporate income tax plus penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit the BC to operate as a shell may be held personally liable for statutory fines, creditors' losses, and fraudulent trading. The UBO can be subjected to travel bans while tax authorities investigate, and foreign criminal courts may imprison the controlling person for tax evasion or fraudulent insolvency.
